title: Migrate query-param versioning to declarative route manifest; remove legacy redirects
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Historically we accepted a query parameter (?v=<version>) on public endpoints to select older runtime routing behavior. That approach causes ambiguous routing, bypasses the declarative route manifest, and prevents consistent rollout observability. This ticket migrates consumers to a single source-of-truth: the declarative route manifest (route.version). After migration we will remove query-param parsing and expunge legacy redirect rules and reconciliation paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All internal and partner routes use route.manifest version field; no production requests routed using ?v= after the monitoring window. 2) Canary (10%) shows <0.1% error-rate delta and p95 latency within 3% of baseline. 3) Route manifest index exists and retrieval latency < 5ms at p95. 4) Cleanup job removes legacy redirect entries and rollout_history entries older than retention period and no linked incidents appear in 14 days.
plan: 1) Audit: run log search for requests with query param v= over last 90 days and produce a consumer list. 2) Reach out to external integrators and internal teams (by Feb 21) with migration timeline and sample manifest entries. 3) Implement compatibility layer in router: if route.manifest exists prefer it; accept ?v only while compatibility flag is on. 4) Dual-write helper: when a route change happens, write both manifest and legacy redirect for 14 days. 5) Start canary on dedicated region at 10% traffic for 48 hours. 6) Ramp to 100% and schedule cleanup window to remove parsing code and redirect table. 7) Post-cleanup monitoring for 14 days.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: downstream partners still using ?v causing 404s. Mitigation: compatibility layer + clear deprecation emails + 14-day dual-write grace period. Risk: accidental routing regressions. Mitigation: small canary, synthetic smoke tests, and automated rollback hook if error-rate increases >0.2%. Risk: config DB index work could impact writes; mitigation: create index in background and monitor DB metrics.
rollback_plan: If canary triggers alerts, flip router to compatibility mode (re-enable query-param parsing) and revert the route fetch change. Post-mortem required before another attempt.
measurement_plan: Primary metrics: fraction of requests with query param v= (target: <0.1% in 2 weeks), router error-rate delta, p95 latency delta. Dashboards: routing-versions-overview and canary-health. We'll capture daily runbook snapshots during canary and post-cleanup.
